title: Replacing Actual Flows with "Clouds" in Architecture
pattern: Failing to capture the origins, resources, and sinks (dependencies) of a data flow, modeling them as infinite or abstract boundaries ("clouds").
why_bad: It creates system blind spots. By assuming a resource is infinitely available or that data goes "away" into a cloud, systems are easily broken when materials run out or backpressure overflows.
detection: Models that register increments/decrements to stock values without tracing the supply pipeline or checking boundary limits.
counterexample:
System tracing that explicitly models bounds and limits:
```rust
fn transfer_funds(source: Account, dest: Account, amount: f64) { ... }
```
source: *Thinking in Systems* by Donella H. Meadows (p. 38-39).
